findings.title: Pause and delete never appear without a ruler rule
findings.body: The list view now computes canPause and canDelete from Grafana Prometheus abilities, but the menu still renders Pause only when rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) is true (line 123) and Delete only when rulerRule is set (line 165). GrafanaRuleListItem and FilterView pass only promRule, so both items stay hidden even for users who are allowed to pause or delete. Those actions are gone from the new alert list; GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx locks this in by expecting exactly four menu items and never asserting Delete or Pause.

findings.title: Silence menu item does not open a drawer
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu shows Silence when the Prometheus-rule ability allows it and calls handleSilence, which only sets showSilenceDrawer. The drawer is still gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule). The new list never passes a ruler rule, so clicking Silence notifications does nothing. The group-loader test only checks that the menu item exists and never clicks it.

findings.title: skipToken still grants Duplicate via Grafana create permission
findings.body: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(skipToken) evaluates useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) instead of returning all-denied abilities. With no rule, loading is false, so MaybeSupported is AlwaysSupported and Duplicate is allowed whenever the user has Grafana AlertingRuleCreate. AlertRuleMenu ORs that result with the ruler result, so cloud and ruler-only rules show Duplicate for anyone who can create Grafana rules, even when the datasource ability denies it. Update and Delete do not leak because their allowed flag stays false, but Duplicate does.

findings.title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities used to set isFederated from isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) and block update, delete, pause, restore, and permanent delete. It now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated to false (TODO on line 243). Every caller of useAlertRuleAbility, including the existing rules UI, will offer edit and delete on Mimir/enterprise federated groups. groupIdentifier does not carry source_tenants, so the check was dropped rather than moved.

findings.title: Filtered Grafana rules are rendered without a list key
findings.body: The grafana branch of the filtered-rule map used to render GrafanaRuleLoader with key={key}. The replacement GrafanaRuleListItem has no key, while the datasource and unknown branches still use key. As infinite scroll appends rows, React can reuse the wrong list-item instance, so action-menu and drawer state can attach to a different rule.

findings.title: Rule links no longer include returnTo
findings.body: The removed GrafanaRuleListItem built the view href with createReturnTo() so the rule detail back link returned to the current list, including filters. The new href is only /alerting/grafana/${uid}/view. Opening a rule from the list and using the in-app back control drops the user on the default alerting page instead of the filtered list.

findings.title: Prometheus abilities treat only alerting rules as exportable
findings.body: useAllRulerRuleAbilities allows ModifyExport, Pause, Restore, and DeletePermanently for any Grafana-managed rule (alerting or recording) via rulerRuleType.grafana.rule. useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates those same actions on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule. The list view relies on the Prometheus hook, so Grafana recording rules lose Export (and would also lose pause/restore/permanent delete once those menu items no longer require a ruler rule).

findings.title: Creating and deleting rules are no longer distinguished
findings.body: GrafanaGroupLoader used to match ruler and Prometheus rules and render ruler-only rules as Creating and Prometheus-only rules as Deleting (without edit or more actions). It now lists only Prometheus rules. Until Prometheus catches up, a just-created rule is missing from the group, and a just-deleted rule still appears as a normal rule with edit, silence, duplicate, and export. The tests that covered those states were removed rather than replaced.

findings.title: isProvisionedPromRule reads provenance on a type that lacks it
findings.body: isProvisionedPromRule takes PromRuleDTO and accesses promRule.provenance after prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule). That helper is not a type predicate, and PromRuleDTO (PromAlertingRuleDTO | PromRecordingRuleDTO) does not declare provenance — only GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase does. This is a TypeScript error, and RuleActionsButtons passes a Rule into this function, so provisioned detection for the clone flow may not typecheck. At runtime a non-Grafana rule short-circuits, but a Grafana rule is only treated as provisioned if the object happens to have provenance.
